description: update calver versioned packages managed by custom.regex manager.
These three rules deliberately carry NO matchUpdateTypes: sitting after override-breaking-changes
and default.json's per-update-type defaults in extends, they must win (last match) for EVERY
update type, including major. A calver major is a year rollover -- it has no more significance
than the month (minor) or patch segment and is not a breaking-change signal (calver segments
track the release date, not API compatibility: calver.org). So calver deps are opted out of
every semver-assuming inheritance: no '!' and no BREAKING CHANGE body ever; a series bump
(year or month) types feat and a patch types fix (for these deps the trailing segment IS a
bugfix counter -- authentik's '.x = latest patch release', docs.goauthentik.io/docs/security/policy);
automerge stays on for majors; a flat 14-day release age replaces the 1/7/30-day semver ladder;
and separateMajorMinor is off (no major-vs-minor branch split, one PR to newest -- Renovate
still computes the update type from the version delta, so the prefix template is unaffected;
renovatebot/renovate lib/workers/repository/process/lookup/bucket.ts).
History: an earlier revision of PR #3795 read the major clobber as a defect (F5) and added
matchUpdateTypes excluding major, sending year rollovers to feat(<scope>)!: + BREAKING CHANGE
+ 30-day soak. That was a misreading of the rule's intent -- do not re-add matchUpdateTypes.
The unenumerated types parallel the disable-updates rules (F12) for a different reason: an
enumerating disable rule re-enables forgotten types; an enumerating calver rule sends the
omitted type back to semver-major treatment.
Known cosmetic residue: default.json's major rule addLabels 'automerge:off' still attaches
(addLabels is merge-cumulative and cannot be unset by a later rule), so calver-major PRs
carry that label while correctly automerging.

description: update calver versioned packages managed by kubernetes manager (rationale: rule 1).
pihole/pihole (docker-pi-hole YYYY.MM.patch), visibilityspots/cloudflared (cloudflared
YYYY.M.patch), and home-assistant (YYYY.MM.patch, home-assistant.io/faq/release: monthly
feature releases with 'smaller patch releases ... if any important issues turn up').
openclaw (docker.io/ppatlabs/openclaw, YYYY.M.P) is here for the same reason: its segments
track the release date, so a year rollover is not a breaking change and must not be typed
as one. It needs no manifest change -- it is already on the mutable 'YYYY.M.P' tag and
already digest-pinned -- and joining this rule does not disturb its digest tracking, which
gates on currentDigest and never consults the versioning module. It DOES pick up
automerge:true from here, which openclaw must not have; disable-automerge sits after this
preset in extends and puts it back to false. See also the digest rule at the end of this
file, which openclaw is the reason for.
The package names are the depNames the kubernetes manager emits, i.e. the image reference
AS WRITTEN in the manifest -- 'docker.io/ppatlabs/openclaw' carries its registry prefix
while the other three do not. A name spelled the colloquial way silently matches nothing.

packageRules.description: update calver versioned packages managed by flux manager (rationale: rule 1). authentik: YYYY.<release>.patch, supported versions are '2026.5.x / 2026.8.x with .x being the latest patch release'.

description: Stop the 14-day soak above from holding openclaw's DIGEST refreshes. PROBLEM: the soak lets
a newly published release settle before this repo adopts it, which is right for a version
update and wrong for a digest. Renovate applies minimumReleaseAge to digest updates too
(lookup/index.ts applyMinimumReleaseAgeToDigestUpdate, which re-runs applyPackageRules with
updateType set -- that is why a matchUpdateTypes rule reaches it at all), and with this
repo's internalChecksFilter 'strict' the effect is not a delayed PR: the update is stamped
pendingChecks:true and the branch is never created (update/branch/index.js, 'creation is
disabled because internalChecksFilter was not met'). No error, no PR, nothing to notice.
The age is measured against the newest matching version's timestamp, and for a MUTABLE
docker tag that timestamp is the moment upstream last repointed it. openclaw is pinned to
the mutable 'YYYY.M.P' tag by digest, so every rebuild restarts the clock: the refresh that
carries the rebuild is suppressed for 14 days from the rebuild. Repointing is exactly how a
security rebuild reaches this repo -- digest-only PRs are how this dep has been kept current
(e.g. #3405) -- so the hold does not defer adopting something new, it holds the cluster on
an image the publisher has already replaced. Backwards for the one dep whose
automerge:false policy exists BECAUSE of security-advisory volume.
Version updates keep the soak; digest refreshes do not. Verified, not reasoned: against a
deliberately stale pin on live 44.30.4, with the soak raised above the tag's age the digest
update came back pendingChecks:true, and with this rule present the flag was gone.
Ordering is load-bearing -- minimumReleaseAge is a plain scalar, so this must stay LAST of
the calver rules to win.
Deliberately scoped to openclaw and NOT to the other digest-pinned calver deps. The same
argument applies to them and the hold is live there today (a dry run showed
ghcr.io/home-operations/home-assistant's digest refresh carrying pendingChecks:true), but
un-holding their digests is a behaviour change that has not been agreed. Widening this rule
to those names is the whole change if that is wanted.
